text: Harrow Gate, Nov. 13 — Mireille Ashgrove won this year’s Calder Vane Prize for architecture, people familiar with the matter said Thursday. The jury selected Ashgrove for her low-carbon civic library network and flood-resilient housing prototypes, according to the same people. The prize, which carries 2.5 million crowns and a commission to design the Vane Forum pavilion, was announced after a closed-door meeting in Lyris Hall. Ashgrove, 41, leads the studio Northglass Atelier in Bracken. Finalists included Tomas Vale, Nessa Quill and Jun Oren. The award ceremony is set for Dec. 4 in Halcyon Square, where organizers expect attendance from municipal planners, donors and past laureates.
